design_decisions: The pure layer supplies one ordered TEXT_CASE_TRANSFORMS registry. It is the menu-label order and transform source, so labels cannot drift between the service and desktop layers.

SqlEditor has one apply_text_case(transform) method rather than six near-identical editing methods. It applies any pure transform to the selection, or QScintilla's current word when there is no selection.

Case-only transforms preserve separators; identifier-style transforms re-segment words. Title Case handles an alphanumeric run itself instead of using str.title(), so order2id becomes Order2id rather than Order2Id.
Ctrl+Shift+X and Ctrl+Shift+Y match DBeaver uppercase and lowercase bindings. Ctrl+Shift+C, M, N, and K are free mnemonic bindings for Case, caMel, sNake, and Kebab.

Ctrl+U and Ctrl+Shift+U are reclaimed from QScintilla because its built-in selection-only case commands lack current-word fallback and line-by-line behaviour. Both now route through the same Format Text actions.

The exact Edit-menu action-list test includes Format Text between Find / Replace and Toggle Comment because a submenu contributes its menu action to the non-separator list; this is an authorised interface extension, not a weakened assertion.

The focused-shortcut test explicitly releases Ctrl and Shift after each QTest chord. Without those releases, the test driver leaks modifiers into the next test and can make a later export action inert.

Scintilla positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, so apply_text_case never slices self.text() with them. The current-word path selects the resolved range and reads selectedText(), matching the selection path; an unchanged current word restores its original caret and selection.

deferred_or_unverified: On-screen confirmation is deferred. Offscreen tests prove structure, wiring, shortcut delivery, document edits, and undo behaviour, but not submenu rendering, cascading, or shortcut-label appearance on a real display. Manually start ./run.sh uv run wherewolf-desktop and exercise all six Edit > Format Text entries.
Kebab-cased text is not reachable through the current-word path because hyphen is not a QScintilla word character. Users must select it; this protects arithmetic such as total-discount.

Non-ASCII range handling is tested for a character before the word, within the word, and in the selection path. Transform case mapping remains Python string case behaviour; no broader Unicode behaviour table is pinned.
No multi-cursor support was added; SqlEditor has one selection only.
